aloevera.watering: Low (Soak and dry technique every 2-3 weeks)
aloevera.soil: Sandy, well-draining cactus or succulent mix
aloevera.toxicity_pets: TOXIC to cats and dogs (Aloctin A & saponins cause vomiting/diarrhea)
aloevera.toxicity_humans: Gel is non-toxic & soothing topically; yellow latex layer is a strong laxative
aloevera.uses: Skin soothing, burn treatment, cosmetics, indoor air purification

banana.sunlight: Full Sun (6 to 8 hours direct sunlight)
banana.toxicity_humans: Completely edible fruit, flower, and stem core
banana.uses: High-potassium staple food, leaves used as eco-friendly food wrappers & plates

mango.watering: Moderate (Deep watering during flowering and fruit development)
mango.toxicity_pets: Fruit flesh is safe; pit/seed contains cyanide compounds and choking hazard
mango.toxicity_humans: Fruit is highly nutritious; tree sap and skin contain urushiol (can cause skin rash)
mango.uses: Fresh fruit, culinary mango dishes, rich in Vitamin C and Vitamin A, shade canopy

papaya.plant_type: Semi-woody large perennial herb / Small tree
papaya.sunlight: Full Sun (Thrives in hot, sunny environments)
papaya.watering: Moderate (Sensitive to waterlogging, root rot occurs in standing water)
papaya.soil: Well-drained porous sandy or loamy soil rich in organic matter
papaya.toxicity_pets: Ripe fruit flesh is non-toxic; seeds and skin should be avoided
papaya.toxicity_humans: Ripe fruit is delicious and healthy; unripe green papaya latex can trigger uterine contractions
papaya.uses: Rich source of digestive enzyme papain, high in Vitamin C, immune booster

corn.sunlight: Full Sun (Requires at least 8 hours of direct sun)
corn.watering: Moderate to High (Crucial during silking and tasseling phases)
corn.soil: Warm, fertile, well-draining loamy soil high in nitrogen
corn.toxicity_pets: Corn kernels are safe; corn cobs are a severe intestinal blockage hazard for dogs
corn.uses: Global food grain, corn flour, biofuel (ethanol), animal fodder

bilimbi.watering: Regular watering; needs moist soil with good drainage
bilimbi.toxicity_pets: High in oxalic acid; excessive consumption can cause kidney issues in pets
bilimbi.toxicity_humans: Edible tart fruit; people with kidney disease should avoid large amounts due to oxalates
bilimbi.uses: Culinary souring agent, traditional medicine for hypertension, rust removal

cassava.watering: Low to Moderate (Extremely drought tolerant once established)
cassava.soil: Sandy or light loamy well-draining soil
cassava.toxicity_pets: TOXIC when raw (Contains cyanogenic glycosides releasing hydrogen cyanide)
cassava.toxicity_humans: MUST BE THOROUGHLY COOKED/SOAKED to remove cyanide before consumption
cassava.uses: Tapioca pearls, gluten-free flour, third-largest source of food carbohydrates in the tropics

coconut.watering: High (Needs ample water, high humidity, and tolerates saline coastal soil)
coconut.toxicity_pets: Flesh and oil are safe in small amounts; excessive oil causes diarrhea
coconut.toxicity_humans: Completely edible and hydrating (Water, kernel flesh, milk, oil)
coconut.uses: Hydrating coconut water, cooking oil, fiber (coir), construction timber and thatch

ginger.sunlight: Partial Shade / Dappled sunlight (Avoid harsh scorching sun)
ginger.watering: Moderate (Keep soil evenly moist, avoid waterlogging)
ginger.soil: Rich, loose, loamy potting soil high in compost
ginger.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic in small amounts; safe spice for dogs in tiny portions
ginger.toxicity_humans: Edible aromatic spice and root vegetable
ginger.uses: Digestive aid, anti-nausea, anti-inflammatory, tea, culinary flavoring

curcuma.watering: Regular watering (Keep root zone moist during active growth)
curcuma.soil: Fertile, loamy, well-draining soil with lots of organic matter
curcuma.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic; curcumin has mild anti-inflammatory benefits in vet care
curcuma.toxicity_humans: Completely safe culinary spice and traditional medicine
curcuma.uses: Golden spice (Curcumin), anti-inflammatory agent, natural yellow dye, antiseptic

cucumber.watering: High (Consistent watering keeps fruit crisp and sweet)
cucumber.toxicity_pets: NON-TOXIC (Excellent low-calorie hydrating treat for dogs)
cucumber.uses: Salads, pickles, skin cooling packs, hydration

eggplant.watering: Moderate to High (About 1 inch of water per week)
eggplant.toxicity_pets: Leaves and stems contain Solanine (TOXIC to dogs and cats)
eggplant.toxicity_humans: Fruit is delicious cooked; raw leaves/stems toxic
eggplant.uses: Global culinary vegetable, roasted dishes, rich in antioxidants

guava.plant_type: Tropical evergreen shrub or small tree
guava.watering: Moderate (Drought tolerant once mature, water during fruit swell)
guava.soil: Adaptable to many soils, prefers pH 5.0 to 7.0
guava.toxicity_pets: Fruit is safe in moderation; seeds can cause mild stomach upset
guava.toxicity_humans: Superfruit exceptionally high in Vitamin C (4x more than an orange) and dietary fiber
guava.uses: Fresh fruit, jams, jellies; guava leaf tea used for gut health

orange.origin: Southern China, Northeast India, Southeast Asia
orange.watering: Moderate (Allow top 2 inches of soil to dry out between deep waterings)
orange.soil: Sandy, slightly acidic to neutral, well-aerated soil
orange.toxicity_pets: Citrus peels, seeds, and oils contain essential oils and psoralens (TOXIC to pets)
orange.toxicity_humans: Fruit pulp is safe, sweet, and rich in Vitamin C
orange.uses: Fresh citrus fruit, juice, marmalade, fragrance essential oils

pineapple.watering: Low to Moderate (Stores water in its thick leaves, drought tolerant)
pineapple.soil: Well-drained sandy loam with acidic pH (4.5 - 6.5)
pineapple.toxicity_pets: Pulp is safe in small amounts; skin and core are tough and choking hazards
pineapple.toxicity_humans: Edible tropical fruit containing the anti-inflammatory enzyme bromelain
pineapple.uses: Culinary fruit, meat tenderizer, bromelain supplements

watermelon.sunlight: Full Sun (Requires hot, long sunny days)
watermelon.watering: High initially, reduce slightly near ripening to concentrate sugars
watermelon.toxicity_pets: Flesh is safe and hydrating for dogs; seeds and rind should be removed
watermelon.toxicity_humans: Extremely hydrating summer fruit (92% water), high in lycopene and citrulline
watermelon.uses: Refreshing fruit, juice, smoothies, seed roasting

spinach.soil: Rich, moist, loamy soil high in organic matter (pH 6.5 - 7.0)
spinach.temperature: 10°C to 22°C (Cool season crop, bolts in high heat)
spinach.toxicity_pets: Contains oxalates; safe in small quantities, avoid large amounts in pets with kidney stones
spinach.toxicity_humans: Nutritional powerhouse rich in Iron, Folate, Vitamin K, and Lutein

peper chili.watering: Moderate (Allow topsoil to dry slightly; overwatering reduces pungency)
peper chili.soil: Well-drained, sandy-loam with plenty of compost
peper chili.toxicity_pets: Contains Capsaicin (Causes severe burning and stomach upset in pets)
peper chili.toxicity_humans: Culinary spice; capsaicin can burn sensitive eyes and skin
peper chili.uses: Culinary heat spice, pain relief creams (topical capsaicin), insect repellent

paddy.watering: Extremely High (Typically grown in flooded paddy fields)
paddy.soil: Heavy clay or silt soil with an impermeable subsoil layer
paddy.toxicity_pets: Cooked rice is very safe (often prescribed for dogs with upset stomach)
paddy.toxicity_humans: Primary global carbohydrate staple feeding over half the world's population
paddy.uses: Staple food grain, rice paper, sake, straw for cattle and paper
